messages:
emma: Quick sync — want to align on the observable event IDs we expose in the console vs the internal URNs. I ran into confusion mapping `auth.login` -> customer-facing label. Should we keep dotted verbs or switch to noun-first labels?

raj: +1. We need a deterministic mapping. Noun-first (e.g., `session.created`) reads better in UIs but our backend currently emits verb-first (`user.login_attempt`).

leah: From an RBAC & product perspective, noun-first helps when building filters: users expect to filter by `session`/`api_key` etc. Also easier to attach resource-level redaction rules.

emma: Good point. Proposal: keep internal URN stable for infra (e.g., `urn:rw:event:auth:user.login_attempt:v1`) and expose a customer label mapping in the consumer contract (e.g., `session.login_attempt`). That way we decouple wording. Thoughts?

dylan: Sounds reasonable. Two concerns: 1) compatibility — how do we roll this without breaking existing consumers? 2) telemetry & KB — make sure dashboards keep working.

marta: For rollout, we can add `exposed_label` to the schema and default it to the previous consumer-visible name. Consumers can opt-in to the new mapping in their ingestion. Plan: emit both fields for 90 days then deprecate one.

raj: Can we see a schema sample? Also need to check KMS-related fields — event-level encryption metadata must not leak customer keys.

emma: Sample snippet below — intended for audit contract and customer docs. Note: all values here are illustrative.

```
{
  "event_urn": "urn:rw:event:auth:user.login_attempt:v1",
  "exposed_label": "session.login_attempt",
  "actor": {
    "id": "usr_123",
    "type": "user"
  },
  "resource": {
    "id": "sess_456",
    "type": "session"
  },
  "outcome": "failure",
  "kms_wrapped": false,
  "meta": {
    "client_ip": "REDACTED_IF_PII",
    "region": "us-west-2"
  }
}
```

leah: Couple notes: 1) `kms_wrapped` should be an enum (`none|customer_wrapped|platform_wrapped`) so consumers can verify how to decrypt if needed. 2) `actor.type` needs enum values defined in the lexicon.

emma: Good catch. Change suggestion accepted. Also: we must ensure `meta.client_ip` is redacted for customer-visible streams unless they passed consent. That ties into privacy & retention.

security-bot: [auditbot] Reminder: retention policy for customer-facing audit events defaults to 90 days. Events flagged `customer_visible=true` require registrar approval for longer retention.

raj: On RBAC: when we change the exposed labels we must update the RBAC rules authoring UI (policy builder). Otherwise admins will see mismatched rule names. Could break canary rules.

marta: We can add a compatibility shim in the policy service: accept both label forms for the deprecation window. Also add a migration job that rewrites saved rules to new labels.

dylan: How about schema evolution? We should publish a matrix: old_name -> new_exposed_label -> valid_from -> deprecation_date. Make it machine-readable (CSV + JSONL) and drop into the model catalog.

emma: Yes. Action items: 1) Security to finalize lexicon of actor/resource enums (@raj, @leah) 2) Eng infra to add `exposed_label` and `event_urn` consistency checks in event linting (@dylan, @marta) 3) Product to approve customer-facing labels and examples (I'll loop product). 4) Docs to produce migration doc and sample queries for Splunk/ES.

leah: I'll draft the enum list today. Also want to flag: event sampling for high-volume routes (e.g., embeddings create) — we need to include sampling metadata so downstream consumers know counts. Suggest `sampling.policy` and `original_count`.

emma: Add that to the schema proposal. Example: `sampling: { policy: "1/10", original_count: 100 }` or similar.

raj: KMS note: never include raw KMS key IDs in customer-visible fields. Use stable references like `kms_ref: "customer:kms#1"` and keep mapping in the control plane with RBAC checks.

marta: Agree. Also add an integration test: ingest a sample event into the customer-facing stream and verify no secret-like fields leak and that `customer_visible` toggles redact PII.

dylan: I'll add lint rule: fail publish if any field value matches regexs for key material or long base64 blobs.

emma: Proposed timeline: RFC this week, 2-week dev sprint for schema + lint rules, 3-week deprecate window (emit both fields), docs + product comms. Any blockers?

raj: Need security sign-off on retention & sampling before RFC lands. I'll take that.

leah: I'll own enums + sample translations.

marta: I'll queue infra work and the migration job design.

emma: Great. One more ask — product wants a few customer-facing examples showing how the event will look in the console and in raw logs. I'll post a short doc after this thread.

dylan: :thumbsup: Add a note about analytics dashboards needing to map old -> new labels, we should provide a helper script.

emma: Thanks all — will post the RFC link in #security when ready.
